## Windows CLI

- Native Windows x64 and ARM64 clients: enrollment, status, remote file
  operations, command execution, and file transfer over TLS and Noise IK.
- PowerShell installer with mandatory SHA-256 verification and user PATH setup.
- Windows runs the CLI client only. Deploy the daemon on Linux or macOS and
  enroll the Windows client with a **bridge** device token.
- Release publication requires Linux tests and native Windows CLI and
  installer tests to pass.

### Install in PowerShell

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest 'https://github.com/pw0rld/agbridge/releases/download/v0.0.4/install.ps1' -OutFile "$env:TEMP\agbridge-install.ps1"
& "$env:TEMP\agbridge-install.ps1" -Version v0.0.4
agbridge enroll --gateway 'wss://relay.agbridge.cloud/' --tls-mode webpki --token 'YOUR_BRIDGE_TOKEN'
agbridge status
```

If local execution policy blocks the reviewed installer, run it with
`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$env:TEMP\agbridge-install.ps1" -Version v0.0.4`,
then open a new terminal to pick up PATH changes.

Alternatively, download `agbridge-windows-amd64.exe` or
`agbridge-windows-arm64.exe`, verify it against `SHA256SUMS`, and rename it
to `agbridge.exe` in a directory on PATH.

## Other Changes and Compatibility

This release includes the working-directory changes from the development branch:

- `agbridge cd` and `agbridge pwd`, with relative remote paths resolved against
  a persisted working directory. Remote paths remain POSIX paths on Windows.
- The daemon advertises `default_working_dir` through its capabilities.
- Root daemon enrollment includes protection against symlink redirection of
  state-directory ownership changes.

**Filesystem policy change:** `default_working_dir` replaces the old path
allowlist fields. It is a starting directory, not an access boundary. Absolute
paths and `..` are allowed; access is governed by the daemon OS user's
permissions. Use a suitably restricted OS account or container when required.
Update deployment configuration accordingly; mixed-version peers may not
support automatic working-directory discovery.
